title: Astro Portal API v1 plan resources

darkness.description: The darkness threshold that bounds this plan's night: the Sun below -18° (`astronomical`), -12° (`nautical`) or -6° (`civil`). ABSENT means astronomical, the planner's own definition; a reader treats any other value as absent (packages/portal/src/planner/state.js `normalizePlanDarkness`).

nightSpan.description: The span of the night this plan keeps: the whole usable night of its `darkness` (`astronomical` mode), or a `custom` span between two UTC instants. ABSENT means `astronomical`. A reader normalises it once (packages/portal/src/planner/state.js `normalizeNightSpan`): an unknown value is dropped; a custom span is rounded to ten minutes, kept between the night's sunset and sunrise, and falls back to `astronomical` when it lasts less than thirty minutes. Shortening the night never deletes a target.

closedAs.description: Additive: the status a device recorded on this plan once it ran its night, before any debriefing: `executed` (every target finished), `partial`, or `abandoned` / `archived` (the person's own gesture on the device). `PUT /v1/plans/{planId}` writes only active plans, so the resource `status` stays `active` and the plan stays writable: the field is what carries a finished night across the plan sync, in both directions. A device sends it whenever the plan it holds is in one of these states, and OMITS it for an active plan (which is how « Reprendre la nuit » clears it). A reader takes the resource `status` when it is not `active` (the debriefing decision froze the plan: it is the authority) and `closedAs` otherwise, so a sync never turns a finished plan back into `active`. `abandoned` is the exception: a night given up needs no debriefing, so the write that sets `closedAs: "abandoned"` (a creation, or a change of the value) is also the decision « Abandonné », taken in the same transaction: the answer reads `status: "abandoned"` with `frozenAt` set, the plan is not in the debrief queue and its next write is refused `409 plan_frozen`. The server stores and serves it untouched, refuses any other value with `400 invalid_payload`, and keeps it through a whole-document save of a browser that does not carry it; a stale write (revision behind) is set aside as ever and never clears it.

archivedFrom.description: Additive: the state an archived plan had before its archive: `executed`, `partial` or `abandoned`. An archive replaces the plan's status, so this is what lets a card say « Abandonné » then « Archivé » instead of « Archivé » alone.

place.description: The plan's observing place, as the web planner and the mobile planner both write it (packages/portal/src/planner/state.js `normalizePlace`). It is what the server derives `nightStartAt`/`nightEndAt` from. Coordinates may arrive as numbers or as decimal strings; `timeZone` is an IANA name and an absent or unusable one is read as UTC, exactly as the planner's own `validTimeZone` does. The whole object stays OPTIONAL: a plan created by a surface that has no place carries none, and its night is then simply unknown.

knownPlace.description: Additive: the link to the known place this place was added from, as in planner/planner-document.schema.json. The known place's details are never stored here.

skyEntered.description: Additive: the sky background the observer typed for the place, as in planner/planner-document.schema.json.

acquisitionLine.description: Additive (« Prise de vue par cible »): one acquisition line a person chose for a plan — the line of the captures' contract (capture.schema.json `proposedAcquisitionLine`) with the same names, units and bounds, plus `binning`, so that what was planned and what was measured compare field by field. Every field is OPTIONAL and an absent one is INHERITED (the target's line, then `item.filter` for the filter of the first line, then the plan's `acquisitionDefaults`, then the suggestion computed on reading — never stored). `filter`: the filter as the person names it (1 to 40 characters, trimmed, never normalised; its family is derived on reading), `null` for « no filter ». `exposureSeconds`: one exposure, in seconds (0.005 for 5 ms). `gain`: the camera's gain, or a camera body's ISO, as an integer; `null` for « the device's own setting ». `binning`: 1 to 8. `frameCount`: the number of exposures; absent lets the time slot decide. Written by the web planner and the mobile planner when the person chooses a value, never by a rule. A write that carries a value out of these bounds is refused `400 invalid_payload` with `error.field` (its path in the payload, `items[0].acquisition.lines[0].exposureSeconds`) and `error.limit`; a field the line does not define is dropped. Every reader (the service, packages/portal/src/planner/plan-acquisition.js `normalizePlanAcquisition`, and the clients) keeps what it understands and discards the rest.

acquisition.description: Additive: the acquisition lines of one target, 1 to 8 (one for a colour camera or a single filter; several for a mono camera, L, R, G, B or Hα, O III, or an alternation of filters). The first line's `filter`, when it is present, is copied into the item's `filter` by every writer and by the service (`null` as `""`), so that a reader that does not know `acquisition` — the iCalendar export, the printable sheet, an installed application of an earlier version — still shows the right filter: the first line wins.

launchedSchedule.description: The plan as it stood when its night was launched (additive): one entry per slotted item, in the order of the slots, with the minutes the item's `startMinute`/`endMinute` held at that instant, counted from the plan's night start. Written ONCE, by the mobile application's launch (`NightSessionController.launchPlan`, before any start of the launch is trimmed), and never rewritten: every surface that saves the plan keeps it as it is. `targetId` is the item's `targetId`, else the item's own `id` (the key the execution screen folds a target by). The execution screen draws every drift of the night against it (the frozen plan), the visual night draws it as its « Prévu » rail; a plan launched without it simply has no frozen reference. ABSENT before the launch.

acquisition.description: Additive: the EFFECTIVE acquisition lines of this item at the instant of the launch — the person's choices and the suggestion resolved, every field the launch knew written — frozen with the slot by the same launch (`NightSessionController.launchPlan`) and never rewritten: the debriefing compares what was measured to them, and a later change of the suggestion rule does not rewrite what was planned. ABSENT for a plan launched before it existed (its debriefing shows the measured lines alone).

ruleVersion.description: Additive: the version of the suggestion rule that resolved the frozen `acquisition`, written with it by the launch.

planItem.description:
One planned target. The write route requires a unique non-empty `id` of at most 200 characters and accepts anything else; the fields named here are the ones a plan written by the web planner or by the mobile planner really carries. `startMinute`/`endMinute`/`durationMinutes` are the step-4 timeline's TIME SLOT, counted in whole minutes from the START OF THE NIGHT — `nightStartAt`, the same origin the planner measures its own timeline from. A zero-length slot (`startMinute == endMinute`) is a real, deliberate value: it is what a catalogue-sourced add produces before the schedule editor places it. `target` is the frozen catalogue snapshot the planner keeps so a later catalogue refresh cannot rewrite the plan. Nothing here is required by this schema: an item from a surface that has no timeline carries no slot at all, and the plan-to-session mapping has an explicit fallback for it.

Phase 6 ter: an item MAY carry `framingId`, referencing an independent framing resource (`framing.schema.json`) instead of embedding one. STORED form (what a client writes): `target` is reduced to `{ id, plannerSource: "framing", framingId }` — any other `target`/`target.framing` content a client sends alongside `framingId` is ignored by the server, never a backdoor to edit a framing through a plan write. SERVED form (what every read hydrates to): `target` is replaced by the framing's own `savedFramingTarget` shape (name included), plus `framingId`, `framingRevision` and `framingState` layered on top. An item whose `target.framing` exists WITHOUT `framingId` (data predating this field) is a tolerated read-only relic: it is neither migrated nor refused, just never treated as a library framing.

projectId.description: Additive: the project — shown as a multi-night plan — this interval works for (`project.schema.json`). The server stores and serves it on every write and read path. When it appears or changes on an item, the write is checked as `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/nights` checks a plan: `403 multi_night_not_active` with `capability: "planner.mosaic"` (also on a private server), `404 project_not_found`, `409 target_mismatch` for an item that is not of the target of that multi-night plan; taking it away detaches and needs the same right. A write that leaves every `projectId` as it was is never checked, and a client without `planner.mosaic` simply shows a normal plan.

filter.description: The item's filter, as the planners have always written it (`""` for none). When `acquisition.lines[0].filter` is present it is the same value (`""` for its `null`), copied by every writer and aligned by the service on every write and read.

acquisition.description: Additive: the acquisition lines the person chose for this target, written by the web planner and the mobile planner; absent while nothing was chosen (every value then comes from the plan's `acquisitionDefaults`, else the suggestion). « Revenir aux suggestions » removes it. Shown and proposed in photography mode only; kept as it is in visual mode. Needs no capability.

payload.description: The plan document as the browser and the mobile planner exchange it. `id` is the BROWSER client id, never the server UUID. Beyond the four required fields it stays open, and the properties named here are the ones the server reads: `location` and `date` derive the night boundaries, `items` carry the time slots, and `equipment` is the night's equipment selection — the frozen plan remains its single source of truth and it is never copied onto a session.

equipment.description: The night's equipment selection, an open object. `windTolerance` (optional): `{ preset: "light" | "standard" | "heavy" | "custom", sustainedKmh, gustKmh }`, the wind and gust limits of the plan's mount in km/h, copied from the device or browser setting of that mount; absent reads as standard. The server stores it as given.

acquisitionDefaults.description: Additive: the plan's defaults — the line the person chose for the whole night (exposure, gain, filter; binning and frame count under « Plus de réglages »), written by the web planner and the mobile planner; a field chosen here holds for every target that does not choose its own, a field left absent stays suggested target by target. ABSENT while nothing was chosen; a reader removes an empty one.

guidedEvening.description: Additive: `true` on the internal plan of a guided evening (an evening with help to aim, a mount or a shared screen), made by the phone for the sake of the data model. It is outside the rule of one plan per night (`planner.multiple`, `409 plan_limit_reached` with `reason: night`) and outside the rule of one place per night (`409 plan_night_place_conflict`): it is never refused by them and never counts for them, and it lives the same night as the night's ordinary plan; it is outside the numeric guard on pending plans (`sync.plan_limit`) too. It is never in the debrief queue and never asked for a debriefing, it is not the plan of the night's execution, and it is shown as « Soirée guidée » (named by its `name`, the evening's title), never as a plan. A phone sends it with `blankExecution: true` and the `guided_evening` event of its session. The service stores it untouched, serves it back, and keeps it through a whole-document save of a browser that does not carry it; omitted or `false` for every other plan.

archivedFrom.description: Additive: written by a device beside `closedAs: "archived"` when it archives a plan, the state the plan had (`executed`, `partial` or `abandoned`), so that a plan archived on a device before the service answers still reads « Abandonné » then « Archivé ». A device omits it for a plan that is not archived or was still planned. The service stores it untouched and serves it back; the resource-level `archivedFrom` is the one a reader takes first.

resource.description: `nightStartAt` and `nightEndAt` are SERVER-DERIVED from the payload's night-of `date` and observing place, with the planner's own definition of the night (Sun at or below -18 degrees, searched from local civil noon). They are read-only: a client never sends them, and a payload that carries fields of those names does not set them. Both are null together when the payload names no usable place or the Sun never crosses -18 degrees that night; the portal then never invents a night. See api/v1.md, section "The night boundaries of a plan". Additive: `sessionMissing` (`true`) and `deletedSessionId` are written only for a plan a debriefing froze (`executed`, `partial`, `abandoned`, or archived after one) that holds **no live session**: its session was deleted or is gone (« Session manquante »). `deletedSessionId` names the deleted session the trash can restore (the one deleted last); without it the session cannot come back and `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/session` makes it again. A plan with a live session, and a plan that was never debriefed, carry neither.

archivedFrom.description: Additive, read-only: the state the plan had before its archive (`executed`, `partial` or `abandoned`), `null` for a plan that is not archived, was archived while it was still planned, or was archived before the service recorded it. A plan the service froze and archives keeps its outcome (`plans.archived_from`); a plan a device archived without the service freezing it (`status` `active`, `payload.closedAs` `archived`) reports the `payload.archivedFrom` the device wrote. A reader takes this field first and falls back to `payload.archivedFrom` when it is absent (a service that predates it); a client that predates it ignores it. Never written: a write that carries it does not set it.

sessionMissing.description: `true` when the plan was debriefed and its session is missing (« Session manquante »).

deletedSessionId.description: The deleted session of the plan that the trash can restore, when there is one.

liveSessionId.description: Additive, read-only: written only for an `executed`, `partial` or `archived` plan that a live session (not in the trash) still names, the oldest one. Such a plan goes to the trash (`DELETE /v1/plans/{planId}`) once no live session names it; until then the deletion answers `403 plan_not_deletable` with `sessionIds`.

executionState.description: Additive, read-only: where the night of this plan stands on a device. `running` — a live session of the plan is open; `paused` — it is open and its last `pause` event has no `resume` after it. ABSENT means `none`: no session of the plan is open (never started, finished, abandoned, debriefed). Derived by the service from the session, never written by a client: a write that carries it does not set it. A surface that reads `running` or `paused` shows the plan as « Nuit en cours » with its `launchedSchedule` read-only, and does not offer to edit, delete or execute it (api/v1.md, « A night that runs on a device »).

executionSessionId.description: Additive, read-only: the open session behind `executionState`; present exactly when `executionState` is.

archiveResponse.description: `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/archive` and `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/unarchive` (D-extra): the plan, archived (`status: "archived"`; its payload, its debriefing and its session untouched) or given back the status it had. `archive` is for a plan the service froze, which `PUT` no longer writes; an active plan is archived by writing it with `closedAs: "archived"` (`409 plan_not_frozen`).

recreateSessionResponse.description: `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/session` : « Recréer la session à partir du plan ». The plan, back to the debriefing (active, not frozen, its closure in `payload.closedAs`), and the session made from it (finished, `origin: "debrief"`, no event, `outcome: null`: « À débriefer »). `409 plan_not_debriefed`, `409 plan_archived`, `409 session_exists` (with the `sessionId`).

deletedPlanEntry.description: One plan of one night in the trash, as `GET /v1/plans/deleted` lists it: the plan as it was (`plan`, the resource with its revision and payload), when it was deleted (`deletedAt`), when the maintenance erases it (`purgeAt`, `deletedAt` plus `graceDays`), the whole days left (`daysRemaining`, rounded up, never below 0), and the multi-night plan it went to the trash with (`projectId`, `null` when it was deleted on its own; restoring that multi-night plan brings it back too).

deletedProjectEntry.description: One multi-night plan in the trash: the resource as it was (`project`), `deletedAt`, `purgeAt`, `daysRemaining`, the plans of one night that went to the trash with it (`planIds`: its nights still to come) and how many nights already run were detached from it (`detachedSessionCount`: they stayed in the Journal as ordinary sessions; its restoration attaches them again when they are still free).

deletedList.description: `GET /v1/plans/deleted` (web session only): the plans of one night (`plans`) and the multi-night plans (`projects`) in the trash, the most recently deleted first. `graceDays` is how long they are kept (30). A read never held by a right.

restoreResponse.description: `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/restore`: the plan back from the trash, its revision up by one (a device's stale copy then conflicts instead of overwriting it).

eraseResponse.description: `POST /v1/plans/{planId}/erase`: the plan of the trash erased for good.

inProgressError.description: `409 plan_in_progress`: the web asked to delete a plan whose night runs on a device. `executionSessionId` is the open session, `lastSignalAt` the last time the service heard of it; `DELETE /v1/plans/{planId}?force=true` deletes the plan anyway and takes that session to the trash with it.

field.description: Additive: with `400 invalid_payload` for a value of the acquisition lines out of bounds, the refused field by its path in the payload (`acquisitionDefaults.gain`, `items[2].acquisition.lines[0].exposureSeconds`, `launchedSchedule[0].ruleVersion`), as a capture's `invalid_metadata` names it.

limit.description: Additive: with `field`, the bound the value crossed (`40` for a filter, `0` or `86400` for an exposure, `8` for a binning or a number of lines), `null` for a type.

deletedPlanIds.description: Additive (SPACE-DATA-MANAGE-01): the ids of the space's deleted plans — in the trash, or deleted before it existed — so that a device drops the copy it keeps of a plan deleted on another surface (a copy with a local edit not sent yet is kept). A plan restored from the trash is in `plans` again and no longer here; an erased plan is no longer named. A reader that predates it ignores it.

oneOf.description: The refused plan write. `versionId` names the set_aside version a stale PUT was stored as. `supplementId` and `sessionId` name the session supplement a PUT to a FROZEN plan that already has a session was stored as instead: nothing is discarded, nothing is rewritten, and the submitted payload is readable again through that session's supplements.
